title: fork()
subtitle: Duplicate address space and fd table — parent waits, child execs
what_you_see: Shell prompt returns only after child exits (unless backgrounded). ls / uses fork+exec internally.
why_it_matters: fork is how Unix composes processes. IR0 clones the address space with copy-on-write, copies the fd table, assigns a new PID, and returns twice — once in the parent, once in the child.

dual_view.kernel:
fork()
  ↓ duplicate mm + fds
  ↓ child: execve
  ↓ parent: wait4

steps.label: Shell requests fork
steps.what_ir0_does: libc clone/fork wrapper before execve for external commands.
steps.why_it_matters: Job control and pipelines multiply fork sites.

steps.label: fork
steps.what_ir0_does: Clone page tables with copy-on-write, duplicate fd table entries, enqueue the child on the runqueue.

steps.label: child execve
steps.what_ir0_does: Child replaces image with /bin/ls or other binary.

steps.label: wait4
steps.what_ir0_does: Parent blocks until child exits; status encodes signal or exit code.
steps.why_it_matters: Zombies exist without wait — PID 1 must reap orphans.
